transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… work’s been getting harder than it should. I keep going back over jobs—checking breakers, labels, torque marks, pictures I took. Sometimes I even drive back to a site to make sure. Simple installs end up taking way too long, and people are starting to notice.
Do you feel anxious when you're checking these things over and over?

Yeah… I do. It’s like I can’t leave it alone. I’ll check the breakers, labels, torque marks, the photos I took… and sometimes I still end up going back to the site. It settles me for a bit, I guess, but it’s gotten to where the job takes way longer than it should.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you're not actively checking things?

Yeah… it does. Even after I know I checked a panel or a disconnect, I’ll get this thought that maybe I missed something—like a loose neutral, or something that could start a fire. I try to push it away, but it kind of follows me home.
Do you feel like you have to perform these checks in a specific way or order to feel okay?

Yeah… kind of. I don’t know if it’s always a strict order, but I end up going back through the same things—breakers, labels, torque marks, the photos—again and again until it feels okay enough to leave. Sometimes it still doesn’t, and I’ll drive back. It makes simple jobs take way too long.
Do you feel like checking these things is necessary to prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah… that’s what it feels like. Like if I don’t go back over the breakers, labels, torque marks, all that, something could be wrong and I’d be the one who missed it. So I keep checking, or looking at the photos, and sometimes I even drive back. I know it makes the job take way too long… people are starting to notice.
Do you feel less anxious after you've completed your checks?

For a little while, yeah. Once I’ve gone back over the breakers, labels, torque marks, the photos… it settles down some. But it doesn’t always last. Sometimes I still feel like I should go back, and that’s when a simple job ends up taking way too long.
Do you feel like you're checking these things to reduce your anxiety?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I tell myself I’m just being thorough, but really I keep going back over the breakers, the labels, torque marks, the photos… and sometimes I’ll even drive back to the site. It calms me down a bit, but it’s gotten to where simple installs take way longer than they should. People are starting to notice.
Are you trying to prevent something specific from happening when you check these things, or is it more about just feeling less anxious in general?

I guess it’s both, but… mostly I’m trying to make sure I didn’t miss something. Like with the breakers or labels or torque marks. I’ll check the photos too, and sometimes I’ve even gone back to the site.

It’s not always one specific thing I can name. It just feels like if I don’t check, something’s going to be wrong, and I can’t let it go.
Do you think you would still feel the need to check these things over and over if someone else, like a colleague, had already checked them?

Yeah… probably. Even if someone else looked it over, I’d still feel like I needed to see it myself. I’d end up checking the breakers, labels, torque marks, the photos… maybe more than once. It’s hard for me to leave it alone, and that’s where the job starts taking way longer than it should.
Do you think your need to check things over and over is because you're afraid of making a mistake, or is it because you just like things done a certain way?

More afraid of making a mistake, I think. It’s not really that I like things a certain way… I just keep going back over the breakers, labels, torque marks, photos, all of it. Sometimes even driving back to a site. It gets out of hand, and then a simple job takes way too long.
Are you finding it difficult to maintain relationships with colleagues or friends due to the time it takes you to complete your work?

Yeah… somewhat. I mean, with colleagues, especially the apprentices, it’s getting harder because jobs I should wrap up in one visit turn into extra checks or callbacks. It throws the schedule off, and I can tell clients don’t always love that.

With friends… I don’t know. I’ve been skipping stuff after work more, because I’m still reviewing a job or thinking I might need to go back. So, yeah, it’s starting to get in the way.
Do you feel like your need to check things over and over is affecting your overall quality of life?

Yeah… I think it is. I don’t really like admitting that, but my schedule’s been slipping. Jobs that should be one visit turn into callbacks or extra checks, and that eats up time with the apprentices and makes clients less confident, I think.

And after work, I’m… not doing as much. I skip things I used to enjoy because I’m still reviewing a job in my head or worrying I need to go back. So, yeah, it’s affecting things.
Do you often worry about everyday things, like your health, finances, or relationships, even when there's no apparent reason to worry?

Not really… I mean, not more than anybody else, I don’t think. I worry about work stuff mostly. The other things—health, money, relationships—I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around worrying about them for no reason.
Do you feel like these thoughts and urges to check things are a part of you, or do they feel like they're coming from outside of yourself?

They feel like they’re coming from me, I guess… not like a voice or anything outside.

It’s more like after I’ve already checked a panel or a disconnect, this thought just barges back in—like, what if I missed one loose neutral, what if something could start a fire. I try to shake it off, but it can follow me all the way home.
Do you think your checking habits are interfering with your ability to enjoy your free time or pursue hobbies outside of work?

Yeah… it is. I don’t really get into much after work lately.

Even when I’m home, I’m still going back over a job in my head, wondering if I need to drive back and check something. So I end up skipping things I used to do. And during the day, it’s messing with the schedule too—jobs that should be done in one visit turn into extra checks or callbacks, and that’s starting to affect clients and the apprentices.
Do you ever have these repeating thoughts or feel the need to check things when you're not at work?

Mostly it’s tied to work.

When I’m not on a job, I still get stuck going back over it in my head… breakers, labels, torque marks, the photos I took. Sometimes I’ll check the photos again, or even drive back to the site if I can’t let it go. It’s not really random stuff at home—it’s the work checks that follow me.
Are there any areas of your life where you feel like you're able to function normally and without these checking thoughts or behaviors interfering?

I guess some things are still okay, but work and after work are where it really gets in the way.

My schedule’s slipping because I turn jobs that should be one visit into extra checks or callbacks. It’s… starting to affect how clients see me, and it takes time away from the apprentices too. And when I’m home, I skip stuff I used to enjoy because I’m still going over the job in my head or wondering if I need to go back.
Do you feel distressed when you're unable to check things the way you want to?

Yeah… I do. I get pretty wound up if I can’t check it the way I want.

It’s like I can’t leave it alone—breakers, labels, torque marks, the photos. I keep thinking I missed something, and then I end up going back over it again, sometimes even driving back. I know it makes the job take way longer than it should… and people are noticing.
Are there any other parts of your life, besides work and free time, where you feel like these checking thoughts or behaviors are causing problems?

Mostly the business side, I guess. My schedule’s getting messed up because I don’t finish when I should… jobs turn into extra checks or callbacks.

And it’s starting to affect clients trusting me, I think. Plus I’m not giving the apprentices the time I should. Outside of that… I’ve been skipping things after work I used to do, because I’m still stuck thinking about the job or whether I need to go back.
